composition_summary: Preserved the single user message unchanged. Proposed one class-22 pure-logic component pc-check-tcp-port-list. The body reads ports with inputs.get('ports') so a missing key yields an invalid result rather than raising, returns an explicit invalid-result object instead of raising, validates every element as a non-boolean integer in 1..65535 before deciding, and assigns result on every branch. Description includes the target input/result contract and the missing typed-runner prerequisite; no UUIDs, host calls, imports or approval claims. The host sink supports class 22 with name/description/content. This is an offline-design draft awaiting Q1, observed behavior and human Q2 before activation.

payload.name: pc-check-tcp-port-list
payload.description: Pure-logic guard that validates a raw candidate TCP-port list before any network action. Target input contract: ports is a nonempty list of exact integers, each in 1..65535 inclusive; booleans are invalid, and missing/null/scalar/empty/wrong-type/out-of-range values fail closed. The outer input contract admits the raw candidate shape while the inner validation implements the rule; this does not relax required-input binding for ordinary Tool usages. Result contract: {valid: boolean, ports: original list if valid else []}. Missing and null remain distinct: a missing key yields an invalid result, not a default. No imports, I/O, host calls or UUIDs. Prerequisite: a typed runner that supplies inputs['ports'] as validated data and executes this body; the target inputs mapping is a target interface, not guaranteed deployed runtime support. This is an offline-design draft; Q1, observed behavior and human Q2 precede activation.

adjusted_volatile_messages: We repeatedly need to reject invalid TCP-port lists before any network action.
